subject: BUG-262 (CRITICAL, PROVEN LIVE): xp and level are directly client-writable in firestore.rules with no value bound
description: PROVEN END-TO-END by Mallory 2026-09-05 during the BUG-255 vote, against PRODUCTION, through the rules-enforced channel rather than an admin token. She created a disposable anonymous Firebase Auth account, wrote a compliant create (xp:0), then issued a raw Firestore REST PATCH with that user's OWN idToken: updateMask xp+level, {xp: 999999999, level: 500} -> HTTP 200. Confirmed by an independent admin-token read of the same doc. She then deleted the test doc and the anonymous account and verified 404 on both channels. THIS BYPASSES EVERYTHING. No Cloud Function, no shaped module id, no house, no allow-list. It is a raw integer write to users/{uid}. Every real consumer of profile.xp reads it directly without routing through syncProgress first: FirestoreManager.js:1006, HouseRenderer.js:2140-2152, ProgressDisplay.js:38, tenant/tenant-data.js:308/690/704. IT SUPERSEDES BUG-255's FIX. The panel voted C (server-derived completion) 3-1, but Mallory's D is correct and complete: server-derived completion is necessary and INSUFFICIENT, because a server that derives XP perfectly is still overwritten by the client's own document update. THE FIX HAS PRECEDENT IN THE SAME FILE. firestore.rules carries a comment recording that ctfBoxesPwned and ctfFlagsCaptured were REMOVED from this identical update allow-list on 2026-08-05 for the same reason. xp and level remain, with a comment claiming they are safe because 'syncProgress CF' overwrites client values, which Mallory demonstrated is a hope and not an enforced guarantee. Fix: remove 'xp' and 'level' from the users/{userId} allow update field list so they become CF/admin-only, exactly as was done for the two ctf fields. REQUIRES A firestore:rules DEPLOY, which is a production write and needs explicit operator authorisation. ALSO NOTED, from the same audit: syncProgress's own 'honest' derivation (functions/index.js:1450-1463, resolveModuleType) validates only string SHAPE and never content existence, so even the supposedly-safe path mints XP for a fabricated module id in a real house. The field-path escape I asked her to check does NOT escape: house='a.b' nests correctly under houseProgress because the literal prefix precedes attacker input; a __proto__ segment returns 500 and fails closed.
